cohort: Every one of the 24 complete programs in the previously frozen semantic calibration cohort. Membership includes historical positives and baseline alerts; this is a diagnostic component, not an unbiased detector evaluation.
hypothesis: A valid contract-relevant prefix can expose a fault even when a later unrelated continuation contains unjustified expectations. Splitting at complete observation statements can reduce semantic review scope while retaining all input composition edits.
policy: Round-robin prefixes in source order, then original fallback. Stop each parent at first controlled failure or failed/unavailable source control. Never select a different prefix based on a manual validity label.
guards: No edit may cross the prefix cut.
Only complete root statements are retained; lexical resource scopes are not split.
At least one source observation remains.
Fresh native controls and independent complete-program audit remain required.
tests: Four focused tests passed across Python, Go and TypeScript, including retained inputs, resource scope, closing syntax and discarded trailing oracle edits.

preparation_failure.reason: Merged calibration cohorts reused display item names. Preparation refused an immutable output collision. The corrected driver assigns cohort-order indexes; no native or provider call occurred in the failed prepare.

limitations: Removing explicit cleanup changes behavior; execute each probe in its own bounded container.
A shorter failing test can still have invalid setup or an invalid oracle.
The component does not establish task recall or replace semantic admission.
